metadata.name: Encryption & Key Management Core Infrastructure
metadata.description: Comprehensive encryption and cryptographic key management system protecting all sensitive data (PDFs, PII, tax documents) at rest and in transit.

purpose.overview: MailMyPDF processes highly sensitive documents (tax returns, immigration paperwork, legal documents, PII). Encryption is not optional — it is the foundational security control protecting user data from unauthorized access, theft, and breach.
purpose.scope: All data handling: at-rest encryption, in-transit encryption, key generation, rotation, storage, and lifecycle management
purpose.stakeholders: System architects, security engineers, compliance officers, backend developers

encryption-at-rest.description: All sensitive data stored in databases or file systems must be encrypted using industry-standard algorithms.

requirements.name: pdf-file-encryption
requirements.implementation: Use NaCl/libsodium or cryptography.io (Python) for AES-GCM
requirements.details: Every PDF uploaded to MailMyPDF is encrypted before storage. File content encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Initialization vector (IV) generated randomly for each encryption. Authentication tag prevents tampering.

example.process:
1. Generate random 96-bit nonce
2. Encrypt PDF bytes with AES-256-GCM using master key
3. Store: encrypted_bytes + nonce + auth_tag
4. Store key reference (key_id) separately
example.output: Encrypted blob stored in S3/cloud storage, unreadable without decryption key

requirements.name: database-encryption
requirements.scope: PII fields: SSN, names, addresses, DOB, account numbers
requirements.implementation: Database-level encryption (PostgreSQL pgcrypto or Transparent Data Encryption)
requirements.details: Sensitive PII fields in database encrypted at column level using AES-256. Application-level encryption alternative if database doesn't support TDE.

requirements.name: temporary-file-encryption
requirements.scope: All temp files created during PDF processing
requirements.implementation: Encrypt temp files immediately after creation, decrypt only in memory for processing
requirements.details: During PDF extraction/processing, temp files may be created. All temp files encrypted immediately. Secure deletion after processing complete.
requirements.secureDelete: Use cryptographic erasure: overwrite with random data 3x before deletion, or use OS secure deletion (shred on Linux, cipher /w on Windows)

requirements.name: backup-encryption
requirements.scope: All database backups and file system snapshots
requirements.implementation: Encrypt backups before storing to S3/backup service
requirements.details: Backups encrypted with separate backup encryption key. Backup key stored separately from application keys. Different key from production encryption enables key rotation without data loss.
requirements.keySegregation: Backup key != application key != archive key

encryption-in-transit.description: All data transmitted between client and server, or server to external services, encrypted using TLS.

requirements.name: tls-encryption
requirements.implementation: Nginx/HAProxy with TLS 1.3 termination, certificate pinning for mobile clients
requirements.details: All HTTP traffic redirected to HTTPS. TLS 1.3 mandatory for all connections. Perfect forward secrecy enabled (ephemeral ECDHE keys). Cipher suites restricted to strong, authenticated encryption only.

certificateManagement.pinning: Certificate pinning in mobile apps to prevent MITM

requirements.name: api-authentication-encryption
requirements.implementation: Every API call requires authentication. API keys transmitted in Authorization header over TLS only.
requirements.details: API keys never transmitted in URL parameters or unencrypted channels. Each API key has expiration date and scope (read/write/delete). Keys rotated every 90 days.
requirements.keyRotation: Automatic rotation every 90 days with grace period for old key

requirements.name: webhook-encryption
requirements.scope: Webhooks sent to external services (Lob, payment processors, etc.)
requirements.implementation: Webhook payloads sent over TLS 1.3, signed with HMAC-SHA256
requirements.details: Receiver can verify webhook authenticity by checking HMAC signature. Prevents webhook spoofing attacks.
requirements.example: Lob mailing service receives webhook: POST with body + X-Signature header containing HMAC-SHA256(body, secret_key)

key-management.description: Cryptographic key generation, storage, rotation, and lifecycle management.

keyTypes.name: master-encryption-key
keyTypes.storage: Hardware Security Module (HSM) or AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS
keyTypes.accessControl: Only key management service can access; application never sees raw key
keyTypes.rotationPolicy: Automatic rotation every 1 year; data re-encrypted with new key

keyTypes.name: database-encryption-key
keyTypes.accessControl: Database server only; application uses KMS API to decrypt

keyTypes.name: backup-encryption-key
keyTypes.accessControl: Isolated from production keys; backup system only
keyTypes.rotationPolicy: Every 1 year; old backups retained with old key

keyTypes.name: tls-private-key
keyTypes.purpose: TLS certificate private key for HTTPS
keyTypes.accessControl: Only web server; never transmitted or logged
keyTypes.rotationPolicy: Automatic with certificate renewal (Let's Encrypt: 90 days)

keyTypes.name: api-signing-key
keyTypes.storage: Application key store (encrypted environment variable or secrets manager)

keyGeneration.method: Use cryptographically secure random number generator (CSPRNG)
keyGeneration.validation: All keys generated using CSPRNG; no weak/predictable key material

production.option1: Hardware Security Module (HSM): Thales, YubiHSM, or similar
production.option2: Cloud KMS: AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault
production.option3: Encrypted key store on secure server with restricted access
production.recommended: Cloud KMS (AWS KMS or GCP) for scalability and audit logging

development.method: Encrypted environment variables or local secrets.json (git-ignored)
development.warning: Never commit keys to Git. Use secret management tools (1Password, HashiCorp Vault, etc.)

keyRotation.policy: All keys rotated on schedule; old keys retained for decryption of legacy data

implementation.step1: Generate new key with same algorithm and length
implementation.step2: Store new key in KMS with version/timestamp
implementation.step3: All new encryptions use new key
implementation.step4: Schedule background job to re-encrypt old data with new key (takes weeks/months)
implementation.step5: Old key retained in archive for decryption of old data
implementation.step6: After grace period (1 year), old key can be destroyed if all data migrated

keyRotation.gracePeriod: Minimum 1 year: old key stays active to decrypt legacy data while new key handles all new encryptions

recovery: Re-encrypt all data with new key (priority: recent sensitive data)
Audit all data accessed since potential compromise
Force password/session reset for all users
Notify users of potential data exposure

key-access-control.principle: Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP): No component has access to all keys

segmentation.access: Can request decryption from KMS; never has raw master key
segmentation.workflow: Application → KMS API (with authentication) → decrypt → get plaintext → process → forget

segmentation.access: Has database encryption key; cannot access file encryption key
Has backup encryption key only; cannot access production key
segmentation.workflow: Prevents backup key exposure from compromising production data

segmentation.access: No encryption keys; logs are encrypted but log system doesn't manage keys
segmentation.workflow: Logs transmitted over TLS to secure log storage

authentication.requirement: All key access authenticated and authorized
authentication.method: IAM policies (AWS IAM, Google Cloud IAM) or RBAC
authentication.audit: Every key access logged: WHO requested WHAT key at WHEN and from WHERE

requirements.name: encryption-verification
requirements.test: Verify all PDFs stored are encrypted (cannot read raw file content)
requirements.method: Read stored file; verify it's unreadable binary (not valid PDF magic bytes)

requirements.name: key-rotation-testing
requirements.test: Verify key rotation works and old data remains accessible
requirements.method: Rotate key; attempt to decrypt old data (should succeed); encrypt new data with new key

requirements.name: tls-verification
requirements.test: Verify all connections use TLS 1.3 with strong ciphers
requirements.method: SSL Labs test; verify no fallback to TLS 1.2; verify no weak ciphers

requirements.name: key-exposure-test
requirements.test: Verify encryption keys never appear in logs, error messages, or memory dumps
requirements.method: Search logs for key material; inspect error messages; memory analysis

keyCompromise.detection: Unauthorized key access detected in KMS audit logs
response: Begin re-encryption of all data with new key (high priority)
Audit all data decrypted with compromised key
Force password reset for all users
Generate new certificate from trusted CA
Deploy new certificate to all servers
Monitor for unauthorized use of old certificate

standards: NIST SP 800-57: Recommendation for Key Management
IRS Publication 1075: Safeguards for Taxpayer Data
PCI DSS: Encryption of cardholder data
compliance.validation: Annual penetration testing and security audit of encryption implementation

implementation.dependencies: Must be implemented before ANY data storage or transmission
libraries: Cloud: AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault
implementation.deployment: Must be in place before production launch; cannot be retrofitted
implementation.testing: 100% encryption coverage: every data write must be encrypted
